summary: Widens referrer_id to BIGINT, backfills orphan references to NULL, then adds a self-referencing FK with ON DELETE SET NULL, enabling safe concurrent operation of old and new versions before retiring the old version.
write_consistency: BIGINT accommodates existing integer referrer_ids. The backfill ensures all non-NULL referrer_id values reference valid account_user rows, so the FK constraint can be added without violation. Old-version inserts of integer values succeed in BIGINT; new-version writes are constrained by the FK. During overlap, setting orphans to NULL preserves data integrity.
revision_notes: Addressed the FK constraint failure by adding a backfill stage that sets orphan referrer_id values (those not present in account_user.id) to NULL before attempting to add the self-referencing foreign key. Previously, the constraint add failed because of rows with referrer_id values absent from the user table.

sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ALTER COLUMN referrer_id TYPE BIGINT USING referrer_id::bigint;

stages.description: Set orphan referrer_id values to NULL
sql: UPDATE account_user SET referrer_id = NULL WHERE referrer_id IS NOT NULL AND referrer_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM account_user);
ALTER TABLE account_user ADD CONSTRAINT fk_referrer FOREIGN KEY (referrer_id) REFERENCES account_user(id) ON DELETE SET NULL;

stages.description: Retire the old version after the schema change is in place.
